description: Least-privilege capability set for the main window (architecture.md Section 9.2). Grants only Tauri's core defaults required for the window to run. The full Phase 5 custom command surface (app_version; conversations: list_conversations/create_conversation/rename_conversation/set_conversation_tags/delete_conversation/get_messages/send_message/set_conversation_route/assign_persona/export_conversation/open_conversation/stop_generation/get_route_explanation; personas: list_personas/create_persona/update_persona/delete_persona; providers: list_available_models/set_provider_secret; permissions: resolve_permission; MCP: list_mcp_servers/add_mcp_server/update_mcp_server/remove_mcp_server/set_mcp_enabled/refresh_mcp_tools/set_tool_permission) is NOT authorized here: in Tauri v2 user-defined `#[tauri::command]` handlers are gated solely by being registered in `generate_handler!` (see src/lib.rs), not by a capability permission token. Capability permissions like `core:app:*` govern Tauri's built-in plugins, which this app does not use, so no plugin permissions are granted. No filesystem, shell, or network capabilities are granted to the webview (Section 9.2 least privilege); all core access flows through the registered commands, which validate every argument and return only display-safe data. Phase 8b adds the minimal permissions the signed in-app self-updater needs and nothing more (Section 9.2 least privilege): `updater:allow-check` (query the GitHub Releases latest.json endpoint), `updater:allow-download-and-install` (fetch + verify + install the signed update), and `process:allow-restart` (relaunch the app after a successful install). No broader updater or process permissions are granted, and still no filesystem/shell/arbitrary-network access is exposed to the webview.
